title: Step 2A Frontend: Multi-day ritual history consumption (latest-first + today awareness)

requirements.summary: Align React Query ritual history fetching and Home/Memories rendering with multi-day, newest-first, limit-based ritual history so latest entry remains ritualHistory[0] while correctly showing today’s completed responses.
acceptanceCriteria: Home page ‘Ritual History’ section can show multiple entries across different days without regressions.
Memories page ‘Load More’ continues to work by increasing the limit and receiving more (older) entries from getRitualHistory(limit).
Home page ‘Both completed!’ section uses the latest entry (index 0) and shows the responses for today when today is complete.

file_operations.description: Harden useGetRitualHistory(limit) to defensively ensure newest-first ordering by entry.date (client-side sort on the returned list) while preserving the limit-based React Query keying/invalidation behavior for incremental loading.

Update the ‘Both completed!’ rendering logic to prefer the ritual history entry for the current calendar day when isComplete is true (falling back to ritualHistory[0] as latest), while keeping the ‘Ritual History’ section mapped across multiple days and continuing to treat ritualHistory[0] as the latest entry.

Ensure Memories ‘Load More’ behavior remains consistent with limit-based history fetching under multi-day storage by relying on the newest-first list and rendering multiple days reliably (no assumptions of single-entry-per-couple).

Extend the Ritual History section checklist to explicitly verify multi-day behavior in the UI (multiple distinct dates, newest-first ordering, and ‘Load More’ returning older entries) without introducing Step 2B-related checks.
